title: Your Phone Motion Sensor Is Reading Your Passwords

vo.en: Your phone knows exactly what you type.

visual.description: Extreme close-up of a man's thumb tapping on a glowing smartphone screen in a dark room.

vo.en: Every tap creates a unique micro-vibration that reveals your finger's exact position.

visual.description: Macro shot of a drop of water creating ripples on a black surface to simulate vibrations.

vo.en: Your gyroscope and accelerometer record these tilts without ever asking for security permissions.

visual.description: A 3D mechanical gyroscope spinning rapidly on a wooden table.

vo.en: Wait until you see how they steal it.

visual.description: A man in a hoodie looking suspiciously over his shoulder into the camera.

vo.en: Researchers proved websites can decode your PIN with 80% accuracy just by tracking motion data.

visual.description: Digital binary code scrolling vertically at high speed on a monitor.

vo.en: Most mobile browsers grant sensor access by default, leaving your passwords wide open to hackers.

visual.description: A hand scrolling through a long list of technical settings on a phone screen.

vo.en: Go to your browser settings and kill motion sensor permissions right now to stay safe.

visual.description: A heavy metal vault door closing and locking securely.

vo.en: Subscribe for more cyber secrets and comment PROTECTED if you checked yours—which is exactly why...

visual.description: A man pointing directly at the camera with a confident smile.
